question: Which of the following sets is unicellular?
solution:
The correct answer is __**egg, sperm**__.

__**Concept:**__

__
 
• **Unicellular **(composed of single-cell) and **multicellular **(composed of many cells).
 
• The cells vary in their shapes. They may be polygonal, disclike amoeboid, thread-like, cuboid or irregular.
 
• The shape cell is always related and vary with the function they perform.

**Explanation:**__

__
 
• The male and the female gametes i.e the** sperm and the egg or ova respectively are unicellular **(single-celled).
 
• They **both are haploid (n) **in nature which undergoes fertilization to form the diploid zygote (2n).
 
• Sperm is the smallest cell in the human body.
 
• Each sperm is a single cell. Sperm is a male gamete that is produced from germ cells.
 
• They are produced by **meiosis**, which results in haploid unicellular cells.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0df9d65250a8862893288415e882c18d11b835ba8b4e9105049a89e7ccd899ad.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

A **zygote (2n)** is **formed after fertilisation by the fusion of a female gamete (egg-n) and a male gamete (sperm-n).** As a result, the **zygote is multicellular. **

To form an embryo, **zygote cells differentiate and divide (mitosis).** The** embryo is a multicellular structure.**
